claims.quote: To provide a fair comparison, we also train a BERT-Small model using the same hyperparameters. We train BERT-Small for 1.5M steps, so it uses the same training FLOPs as ELECTRA-Small
claims.reason: Abstract and introduction explicitly propose replaced token detection as their new pre-training task. BERT-Small is retrained with the same hyperparameters and matched FLOPs, a controlled with-vs-without comparison of the objective, so ablation is YES.

claims.quote: First, we find that ELECTRA is greatly benefiting from having a loss defined over all input tokens rather than just a subset: ELECTRA 15% performs much worse than ELECTRA.
claims.reason: Introduction states as a key advantage that the discriminator learns from all tokens rather than the masked subset. ELECTRA 15% is identical except the loss is restricted to 15% of tokens, a matched ablation, so YES.
Weight tying is a Section 3.2 experimental extension, not a contribution stated in the abstract, contribution list, or introduction. Not a distinct headline ARCH claim under the location rule.
Generator-size 1/4–1/2 is an empirical hyperparameter finding in Section 3.2 (‘we find’), not a novel ARCH contribution claimed in the abstract or introduction.

Joint MLE vs two-stage/adversarial is a negative experimental comparison in Section 3.2, not a separate novelty claim in the abstract or introduction; the MLE generator is part of the main RTD method already covered.
Same TRAIN contribution as A_only0 (replaced token detection, including learning at all positions). Not a distinct additional claim; all-token loss is already isolated as A_only1.
